findings.summary: WT15 is NOT fixed: every row in both selection suites still passes exactly one changed path, so neither the shared-build escalation nor the multi-path mapping is constrained. A real commit touches many paths. Confirmed green against the real 38-test Gradle suite for all three mutations below. Reinstating the exact historical shape (printf '%s\n' "$@" | grep -qE ...) at line 96 also leaves the suite green -- the regression this suite's own javadoc exists to prevent is reintroducible in silence (rc=141 reproduced for that predicate shape standalone at ~5000 paths). Fix: add one row with two paths, e.g. 'docs/a.md gradle/libs.versions.toml' expecting shared-build/ALL, and 'client/A.java format/B.java' expecting two modules.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:96 `for p in "$@"` -> `for p in "${1:-}"` (SURVIVES; `--plan docs/a.md gradle/libs.versions.toml` then prints WHY=module-dirs / MODULES= i.e. 'ok no module changed' on a shared-build change). AND scripts/check-module.sh:83 `printf '%s\n' "$@"` -> `printf '%s\n' "$1"` (SURVIVES; `--select-modules ... client/A.java format/B.java` returns only `client`).

findings.summary: Answering 'did collapsing --plan into plan() buy what I intended': only partially -- a mutation INSIDE plan() still survives. The MODULES assertion uses substring `contains` and is not line-anchored; for the docs row `want` is "" so it degenerates to contains("MODULES="), which every possible output satisfies (verified: under mutation the row printed MODULES=docs and stayed green). Same defect on non-empty rows: contains("MODULES=format") is satisfied by "MODULES=format sequencer". Fix: extract the MODULES= line from the output and isEqualTo it.
findings.surviving_mutation: Append to plan() at scripts/check-module.sh:124: `[ -n "$PLAN_MODULES" ] || PLAN_MODULES="$PLAN_ALL"`. Confirmed GREEN on the real 38-test suite. Every docs-only commit then builds all eight modules, falsifying the 'a docs-only commit pays NO Gradle startup' claim added to .pre-commit-config.yaml and build.md in this same diff, with nothing red.

findings.summary: plan()'s drift VERDICT has no failure-path test (testing.md rule 14). Every row asserts DRIFT=ok; no test ever observes DRIFT=fail. ModuleDriftTest covers the --check-drift door's exit status (line 158), which is a different code path from plan()'s verdict computation (line 117), so it does not cover this. The gate consumes the verdict at line 193 (`[ "$PLAN_DRIFT" = ok ] || finish`), so under the mutation drift never halts the gate. Fix: a --plan invocation against a drifted tree, or let plan() take the settings path so a fixture can reach it.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:117 `if [ "$FAILED" -eq "$before" ]; then PLAN_DRIFT=ok; else PLAN_DRIFT=fail; fi` -> `PLAN_DRIFT=ok`. Confirmed GREEN on the real 38-test suite.

findings.summary: The gate-path orphan candidate SOURCE is executed but unconstrained -- and it is inside plan()'s callee, not in the four lines named as uncovered by the M0.22 comment. ModuleDriftTest always injects the candidate list via --check-drift's third argument, so the `[ -n "$candidates" ] || candidates=$(workspace_files ...)` default (lines 63-64) is entered only by --plan and the gate, where nothing reflects its result: `checked=N` counts only the first loop. Note the loop BODY is bound (deleting the buildSrc skip at line 67 is correctly killed by the DRIFT assertion) -- it is the source that nothing pins. Consequence: a tracked module directory with a build.gradle.kts and no settings entry is silently unchecked, which is the 'a short list is indistinguishable from compliance' defect this half of the gate exists to prevent.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:63 `candidates=$(workspace_files '*/build.gradle.kts' | grep -E ...)` -> `candidates=$(true | grep -E ...)`. Confirmed GREEN on the real 38-test suite.

findings.summary: Answering 'would checked=8 hardcoded pass': yes. The literal 8 is never related to the derived module count -- ALL= and checked= are two independent literals in the same assertion. Minor rather than major because two real mitigations exist: the `unrun` sentinel at line 113 kills 'check_drift never called', and shrinking the loop input (`for m in ${all%% *}`) yields checked=1 and is killed. So the counter does bind iteration count unless the counter itself is faked. Fix: parse the ALL= line from the same output and assert checked equals its word count.
findings.surviving_mutation: scripts/check-module.sh:49 `DRIFT_CHECKED=0` -> `DRIFT_CHECKED=8`, and delete the increment at line 51. Confirmed GREEN on the real 38-test suite.
